# Intro

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(here)
import_directory<-paste0(here(),"/blog/2026-08-25-qgis-shipping")
```

The Baltic Sea is one of the busiest seas in the world, with sea transport accounting for 15% of global sea freight ([Rutkowsky & Kubacka 2023](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-36114-3))

In addition, the construction and maintenance of OWFs is further associated with a strong increase in shipping activities in and around OWFs ([Exo et al., 2003](https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=3216&context=wsg_bulletin)).

In this blog post, we'll explore how add a shipping information from a tif file in QGIS. 

## Shapefile

To download shipping traffic data go to EMODnet Map Viewer > Catalogue > EMODnet Human Activities > Vessel density > Monthly totals 2017-2023 > All Types > Click on the “i” icon > Select Download.

A zip file named “EMODnet_HA_Vessel_Density_all_2017-2023 would be downloaded. For the period of December 2023, the raster information is under vesseldensity_all_20231201.tif.

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(import_directory,"/EMODnet.png"))
```

## Load

Load the files (tif) from 20230101 to 20231201 in QGIS.
Once loaded, change Style for better visualization.
In this example, under Singleband Pseudocolor, I selected 9 classes with a continuous classification. I then manually adjusted the class breaks and color scale to better represent the vessel density values.

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(import_directory,"/symbology.png"))
```

Once the style is defined, go to Styles > Copy Style > All Style Categories to copy the complete styling configuration.

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(import_directory,"/copy_style.png"))
```

For the other layers, go to Styles > Paste Style > All Style Categories to apply the copied styling configuration.

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(import_directory,"/paste_style.png"))
```

## Layout

In this example, I selected the vessel density color scale, EEZ, Natura, and OWF layers (see previous posts for how to add this polygons using QGIS). For the OWF layer, I displayed only projects that are currently in production or under construction. Interestingly, the OWF show high densities of shipping traffic. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(import_directory,"/BalticSea_08shipping.jpeg"))
```
